newsitem.title: CHINA: China says won't return to controls on yuan.
newsitem.headline: China says won't return to controls on yuan.

text.p: China will not re-impose controls on the convertibility of its currency unless it sees a worsening of its payments position, the official Xinhua news agency said on Monday.
China said its currency became freely convertible on the current account as of Sunday, though it retained controls on the capital account.
The Xinhua news agency, quoting an official for currency regulation, did not give further details of how much of a deterioration would be required before controls would be imposed again.
Beijing appeared to see this prospect as remote, and the news agency said the state's macro-economic controls continued to gain strength.
Xinhua said that companies that wanted to buy or sell foreign exchange still needed to go to specified foreign exchange banks and provide required documentation.

Individuals who wished to go abroad on private visits would also face limits on the amount of foreign currency they could exchange. The limits could be exceeded in cases where the need for additional amounts could be justified.
